Karthik / Markus —

High level: mutuality is our preferred default (mutual exclusion of consequential, special, incidental, punitive damages) because it limits asymmetric exposure and is consistent with other enterprise MSAs we’ve signed. One-way exclusions increase litigation risk and create bad precedent.

If Commercial needs to concede, these are the guardrails I recommend to send back as a compromise:

1) Mutual exclusion with narrow defined exceptions: willful misconduct, fraud, breach of confidentiality, and indemnity obligations.
2) Definition of "Consequential Losses" should be illustrative not exhaustive; include specific line items we’re comfortable excluding (e.g., lost profits, loss of business, loss of use, downtime-related third-party claims) but exclude amounts payable under third-party claims that we indemnify.
3) Cap: propose a monetary cap equal to the fees paid in the prior 12 months under the Order Form (12-month cap). If Acme insists on 24-month, ask for compensating concessions (longer payment terms or higher overage fees).
4) One-way? If forced, narrow to customer-only (no carve-outs for third-party indemnities) and preserve our right to recover indemnity-related damages.

Draft language attached in the extract I pulled into msav2-damages-extract.pdf.

I can join the call with their counsel — recommend 30m to walk through definitions and agree exceptions.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Their commercial lead is sensitive to unlimited exposure in the indemnity bucket.

They are also concerned that an "illustrative" definition of consequential could later be interpreted broadly in discovery. They prefer a more prescriptive list.

- In parallel, Acme will share a short memo on why one-way is commercially necessary for them (will circulate before the call).

Team — thanks. Call scheduled for Thursday 10am PT (calendar invite with dial-in sent). Quick plan ahead of the call:

1) Laura — please bring the 12-month cap language and the alternative 24-month + commercial concession suggestion.
2) Markus — be prepared to call out product-level mitigations (SLAs, limits on data retention) that lower our residual risk.
3) Sofia / Acme — please circulate Acme's memo on why a one-way exclusion is commercially necessary so we can review before the call.

Suggested compromise to propose on the call (can finalize after):
- Keep a mutual exclusion of consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages, but explicitly preserve damages arising from: (i) willful misconduct/fraud, (ii) breach of confidentiality, (iii) obligations to indemnify for third-party claims; and (iv) amounts required by law.
- Monetary cap = greater of (i) fees paid in prior 12 months or (ii) $250,000 for initial term — adjustable by Order Form.

If Acme won't accept mutuality, we should ask for: (a) expanded indemnity carve-outs, (b) higher cap, and (c) a short repricing credit for the incremental risk.

I'll lead the call and try to keep us focused on definitions and business tradeoffs.

— Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
